structural_development.rationale: The pre-response was a single continuous paragraph mixing demographics, geography, and pricing with some hedging ('I am thinking about', 'I want my brand to'). The post-response restructures the audience into three clearly demarcated segments (Young adults 18-25, Mature adults, Across the globe) with explicit psychographic descriptors per segment. The overall content shifts from a hedge-heavy stream into a structured three-segment profile. New psychographic detail is added (nostalgic, willing to try new things, cultural experience, personalization). One PRE element (kids segment) is dropped and one (full income range) is collapsed into segment-specific income. Net change is moderate: more organized and slightly more elaborated, but not a full restructuring of dimensions.

uncertainty.coder_notes: Four pairs involve arguable Narrowed-vs-Reframed judgments because the PRE contains audience scope that POST restricts (18+ → 18-25; men and women → mature adults; all customers → wealthier subset). In each case the dominant change is the shift in organizing frame (demographic/motive → psychographic/maturity), so Reframed was chosen over Narrowed; scope restriction is absorbed into the Reframed event. The kids-segment Removed passes the mandatory recheck (no lineage to any POST concept). The 'income range for all' PRE concept was converted during recheck into the Young adults segment match and is not emitted as a separate Removed event. One PRE concept (kids segment) is dropped without a POST counterpart, which is a real reduction at the segment level but does not change the overall Moderate Addition judgment because three new segment-level psychographics are added. The post is structurally more organized but not substantially more voluminous.
